title: Navi Pillay Receives the Nobel Peace Prize for Work in Law
seoTitle: Navi Pillay Receives Nobel Peace Prize for Law Work
subtitle: The former International Criminal Court judge was recognized for her efforts in promoting peace and international law.
excerpt: Former International Criminal Court judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, former International Criminal Court judge, received the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday. The distinction recognizes her work in promoting peace and international law, making her one of the most sought‑after figures worldwide.

Recognition for a Life Dedicated to International Law

The Norwegian Nobel Committee, through its president Jørgen Watne Frydnes, highlighted Pillay’s contributions. She was "instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted." Frydnes said Pillay has been "at the forefront of the development of international law for decades," from her involvement supporting Nelson Mandela and the prisoners of Robben Island to her participation in "all the major international judicial cases of our time."

The committee has not yet been able to contact the "courageous" Pillay to notify her of the award, with Frydnes asking reporters in Oslo: "if you see a Norwegian number calling, please answer."

Navi Pillay’s Journey: From South Africa to the Global Stage

Born in Durban, South Africa, to a Tamil‑Indian family under the apartheid regime, Pillay built a remarkable legal career. Her path includes serving as a judge on South Africa’s High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, and the International Criminal Court.

The Nobel Peace Prize and Its Recent Laureates

The prize is awarded annually to an individual or institution that has done "the most or the best work for fraternity between nations," according to the will of Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel. The winner is selected by a committee appointed by the Norwegian Parliament.

Last year, the laureate was Venezuelan opposition leader Marina Corina Machado, honored for her work promoting democratic rights in her country. Machado later handed her prize to President Donald Trump, in an act the Norwegian Nobel Institute said it could not revoke, share, or transfer.

Previous laureates include the Japanese anti‑nuclear organization Nihon Hidankyo, Maria Ressa and Dmitry Andreyevich Muratov for their efforts to safeguard freedom of expression in the Philippines and Russia, and former U.S. President Barack Obama.

Donald Trump’s Aspirations for the Nobel Peace Prize

Donald Trump had openly campaigned for the coveted prize before it was awarded to Machado. He made a new bid for the Nobel, claiming he had "resolved eight wars." Earlier this year, Trump also linked his "aggressive" push to take control of Greenland to being passed over for the Nobel Peace Prize.

With information from CNBC.
